Barely touches waxy mealybugs and kills their wasps and lady beetles, so outbreaks follow.
prevent: Check seedlings, cuttings and fruits from other farms before they come in. Mealybugs ride on planting material.
Cut off and bag heavily infested shoots and fruits, and wash small colonies off with a strong jet of water.
Keep ants off with sticky bands on the trunk and by breaking their nests. Ants guard mealybugs from their enemies.
Weed the farm and its edges. Many weeds carry mealybugs between seasons.
Do not overfeed with nitrogen. Soft new growth breeds more mealybugs.
Clean tools, sacks and shoes after working in an infested block.
bio: Tiny wasps such as Acerophagus papayae can crash papaya mealybug numbers. Brown puffed mealybugs mean they are working.
Lady beetles (including the mealybug destroyer), lacewings and hoverfly larvae eat mealybugs. Avoid broad sprays.
Beauveria bassiana or Lecanicillium sprays infect mealybugs in humid weather.
pests.threshold: Each week look at 10 plants or trees per block: shoot tips, leaf joints, undersides and fruit stalks. Treat single colonies by cutting or washing them off. Spray a block only when colonies spread to many plants and you see few brown, puffed up parasitized mealybugs.
pests.rotate: Citrus mealybug and other mealybugs have resisted organophosphates and pyrethroids in other countries. Rotate spirotetramat (23), buprofezin (16) and a neonicotinoid (4A) with oils or soaps, and keep broad sprays out.

pests.name: Oriental fruit fly
pests.hint: Small sting marks on the fruit skin where the female laid eggs.

mango: Use it as the protein bait spot spray: a splash on the leaves of each tree, not a cover spray on the fruit.
A cover spray reaches few flies, leaves residue on fruit and kills the wasps that parasitize the maggots.
A cover spray reaches few flies, leaves residue on fruit and kills bees and natural enemies.
Old broad cover spray. Kills bees and natural enemies and can bring mites and scales after it.
Very toxic and leaves residue in fruit. Many countries stopped its use on fruit. A last resort only.
Old broad carbamate, toxic to people, bees and fish. A last resort with the full waiting time.

prevent: Bag the fruits at least 6 weeks before harvest so the females cannot sting them.
Pick up fallen and overripe fruit every 2 to 3 days. Bury it deep or seal it in a plastic bag in the sun.
Harvest at the mature green stage when the buyer allows. The flies prefer soft ripe fruit.
Kill the males: blocks or wicks with methyl eugenol and a killing agent, spread over the whole area, cut mating.
Clear wild host trees and unpicked fruit near the orchard, and work with neighbors, since the flies travel between farms.
Prune the canopy open. Bagging, bait spots and checks are easier on low, open trees.
bio: Native parasitic wasps attack the eggs and maggots in the fruit. They survive where cover sprays are few.
Weaver ants (hantik) patrolling the canopy cut fruit fly stings on mango. Leave their nests on the tree.
Ants, beetles and chickens eat the maggots and pupae in the soil under the trees.
pests.threshold: Hang methyl eugenol traps from flowering and count the males each week. When the catch climbs as the fruits near maturity, start bait spot sprays and daily pick up of fallen fruit. Also cut open 10 fruits with sting marks: maggots inside mean the fruit on that tree is already hit.
pests.rotate: In Asia the oriental fruit fly resists organophosphates such as malathion and trichlorfon and pyrethroids such as beta cypermethrin, and spinosad resistance has shown up where bait was used alone for years. Lean on sanitation, bagging and male traps so bait sprays stay few, and swap the bait's insecticide group when a choice is registered.

pests.name: Coconut scale insect (cocolisap)
pests.hint: Small flat scales crowd the underside of the leaflets.

coconut: Given by trunk injection on infested palms by trained teams. Keep the waiting time before you pick nuts or tap sap.

prevent: Never carry coconut seedlings, fronds, husks or ornamental palms out of an infested area. That is how cocolisap spread.
Cut the badly crusted lower fronds and burn or bury them on the spot, before the crawlers move on.
Report the first yellowing palms to your local agriculture office at once, so wasp releases can start early.
Do not spray broad insecticides on the palms or on the crops under them. It kills the wasps and lady beetles doing the work.
Fertilize and weed the palms well. A well fed palm survives an attack and recovers faster.
bio: The native wasp Comperiella calauanica parasitizes cocolisap and brought the outbreaks down. Protect it and ask for releases.
Small lady beetles and other predators eat the scales and their crawlers. Leave them be.
pests.threshold: Each month, turn over the lower leaflets of palms near any known outbreak and look for crowded flat scales. Act at the first palms with crusted leaflets and yellowing lower fronds: cut and destroy those fronds and report them. Scattered scales with many dead or parasitized ones need no chemical.

pests.name: Coconut rhinoceros beetle
pests.hint: Leaflets show V shaped or wedge shaped cuts when the frond opens.
pests.no: Spraying tall palms does not pay. Clean up the rotting logs, stumps and heaps where the beetle breeds.
prevent: Cut fallen and dead palms and old stumps into pieces, then split, burn or bury them. Rotting trunks are where the grubs grow.
Turn, spread or use up heaps of compost, manure, sawdust and coconut husks, or cover them with fine net so beetles cannot lay eggs.
Grow a creeping cover crop over cut logs and stumps at replanting. Shaded logs draw far fewer beetles.
Pull the beetle out of its hole in the crown with a hooked wire and kill it, then fill the hole with sand.
Hang pheromone traps 1 to 2 km apart to watch numbers, and empty them often. More traps near breeding sites catch more beetles.
bio: Spread the green muscardine fungus (Metarhizium) into breeding heaps and logs. Grubs that pick it up die and pass it on.
Where it is offered, release beetles carrying the Oryctes virus. It spreads in the breeding sites and keeps numbers down for years.
pests.threshold: Each month look at the newest opened fronds of young palms. Fresh V shaped cuts, or a bored hole with chewed fiber at the base of the spear, mean beetles are feeding and a breeding heap is close by. A pheromone trap catch that keeps rising tells the same.

pests.name: Coconut leaf beetle (Brontispa)
pests.hint: The still folded spear leaf shows thin red brown streaks along its leaflets.
pests.no: Sprays seldom reach the beetles inside the folded spear and kill their enemies. Earwigs, wasps and clean seedlings control it.
avoid: Pyrethrum
Kills the earwigs and wasps that control Brontispa, seldom reaches beetles in the folded spear, and no label names it.
Rotenone (from derris)
Kills fish and is no longer allowed on food crops in many countries. Earwigs and wasps work better.
prevent: Inspect seedlings and ornamental palms before moving them. Brontispa travels mostly on planting material.
Cut and burn spear leaves crowded with larvae on young palms and in the nursery.
Water and feed young palms well so the spear unfolds fast. The beetle lives only in the folded spear.
Keep earwig homes: leave some leaf litter and husks near the palms and do not spray the crowns.
Where both are planted, local tall types tend to suffer less than some dwarf types.
bio: Put earwigs (Chelisoches morio) into the spear leaves. They hunt Brontispa eggs and larvae and can be reared cheaply.
The wasps Asecodes hispinarum (on larvae) and Tetrastichus brontispae (on pupae) parasitize Brontispa and bring outbreaks down.
Metarhizium anisopliae sprayed into the spear leaf infects larvae and adults in wet weather.
pests.threshold: Each month open the spear leaf of young palms and nursery seedlings. Beetles, flat larvae or fresh brown streaks in the folded leaflets mean act now with earwigs and by removing the worst spears. Seedlings and palms under 5 years suffer most.

pests.name: Red palm weevil
pests.hint: Holes appear at the base of the fronds or in the trunk.
avoid: Fipronil
Very toxic to bees, fish and the earwigs that eat weevil grubs, and no label names this weevil.
prevent: Do not wound the trunk: cut no climbing steps, and cut green fronds about 120 cm from the trunk.
Seal any trunk wound or cut at once with tar or mud. The females lay eggs in fresh wounds.
Cut down palms past saving, split them and burn or bury them, so the grubs inside cannot become adults.
Treat bud rot and rhinoceros beetle holes early. The weevil lays eggs in the wounds and rotting tissue they leave.
Trap adults with a pheromone lure in a bucket baited with sugarcane, or a split log with toddy, and kill the catch each week.
Clean rotting debris out of the leaf axils and crown now and then.
bio: Earwigs and assassin bugs eat the eggs and young grubs. Avoid spraying the crowns.
Weevils caught in traps can be killed with Beauveria or Metarhizium fungus instead of poison.
pests.threshold: Walk the palms each month and look for holes oozing brown liquid with chewed fiber at the trunk or frond bases, a wilting spear leaf, or a gnawing sound when you put an ear to the trunk. Act on the first palm you find, and look harder at its neighbors. A rising trap catch means more palms are being hit.

pests.name: Banana weevil
pests.hint: Tunnels run through the corm and the base of the pseudostem.

banana: Use the granules at the base of the mat only. Injecting fipronil into the banana bud is banned.
Spray the stem base and mat or drench the soil. Very toxic to fish, so keep it out of canals and ponds.
Very toxic to people, birds and fish. A last resort, never near water or where animals graze.
Very toxic, and mainly a nematode product. Weevil control is a side effect.

prevent: Plant tissue cultured plantlets, or pare suckers down to clean white flesh and throw out any with tunnels.
A hot water dip of pared suckers, about 53 to 55 C for 20 minutes, kills grubs and eggs and also nematodes.
After clearing an old field, rest it or grow another crop as long as you can before banana again. A year beats 3 months.
Cut harvested stems at ground level, chop them and spread the pieces to dry. Rotting stumps breed weevils.
Lay split pseudostem traps cut side down by the mats, collect the weevils every few days, and change the traps every 2 weeks.
Desucker on time and keep old corms out of the field, so adults find fewer places to lay eggs.
bio: Beauveria bassiana put on the cut face of pseudostem traps infects the weevils that come, and they carry it to others.
Predatory beetles (Plaesius) and some ants eat weevil eggs and grubs in the mat. Avoid soaking the soil with broad insecticides.
pests.threshold: Each month lay 10 split pseudostem traps per block beside the mats and count the weevils under them after 3 to 5 days. At harvest, pare the corms of 10 cut mats and look for tunnels. A catch that climbs month after month, or tunnels in many corms, means clean the field and treat the mats.
pests.rotate: Banana weevils have resisted cyclodienes, organophosphates and carbamates in other banana countries where one soil product was used for years. Rotate fipronil (2B), bifenthrin (3A) and imidacloprid (4A), and let clean suckers and traps carry most of the load.

pests.name: Banana aphid
pests.hint: Dark red brown aphids sit in colonies on leaf undersides, sheaths and young suckers.

banana: Kills bees. Spray a bunchy top plant and its neighbors to kill the aphids before you cut the plant.
Kills only the aphids it wets. Aim at the leaf sheaths and sucker bases.
Old broad spray. Kills the lady beetles and wasps that feed on the aphids.

avoid: Buprofezin
Does not work on aphids. It is made for hoppers, whiteflies and mealybugs.
Bifenthrin plus buprofezin
A treated bunch bag. Banana aphids live on the plant base and suckers, so the bag does not reach them.
Deltamethrin
Banned on banana.
prevent: Plant only clean, virus free planting material such as tissue cultured plantlets from a trusted nursery.
Kill the aphids on a bunchy top plant first, then kill the plant and its suckers and chop it where it stands.
Never move suckers out of a field or town with bunchy top.
Clear volunteer bananas, heliconia and canna near the farm. They shelter the aphids.
Desucker often. Aphids crowd on young suckers and new growth.
Check every 2 weeks and rogue sick plants at once, together with the neighbors, since the aphids fly between farms.
bio: Lady beetles, lacewings, hoverfly larvae, small wasps and many spiders feed on banana aphids. Avoid broad sprays.
Ants tend the aphids at the plant base. Keeping ants down lets the predators work.
Beauveria bassiana and Lecanicillium infect aphid colonies in humid weather.
pests.threshold: Every 2 weeks check the leaf sheaths, the base of the pseudostem and the young suckers of 20 plants per hectare. One aphid can carry bunchy top, so do not wait for big colonies near any sick plant: treat the aphids there, then rogue.

pests.name: Mango leafhopper
pests.hint: Wedge shaped hoppers jump and fly with a clicking sound when you shake a flowering branch.

mango: Stops hoppers feeding and spares spiders and lady beetles. Best sprayed as the flower buds push out.
Works on the young hoppers only, not on the adults already in the flowers. Spray early, as buds push.
Kills bees and flies that pollinate mango: spray it before the flowers open, never at full bloom.
Kills bees and flies that pollinate mango: spray it before the flowers open, never at full bloom.
Hoppers in heavily sprayed mango areas grow less sensitive to it. Rotate, and spray before the flowers open.
Kills bees and flies that pollinate mango: spray it before the flowers open, never at full bloom.
Mild. Slows young hoppers but needs repeat sprays when numbers are high.
Mild and kind to natural enemies. Do not spray it on open flowers or in the midday heat.
Broad spray that also kills spiders and lady beetles. Keep it for a high count before bloom.
Broad spray that also kills spiders and lady beetles. Keep it for a high count before bloom.
The pyrethroid half kills natural enemies and the neonicotinoid half kills bees. Use only before bloom.
Old broad spray that kills bees and natural enemies and can bring mites and scales after it.
Old, toxic organophosphate. A last resort only, with the full waiting time before harvest.
Very toxic old organophosphate. Keep it as a last resort and keep the waiting time before harvest.

prevent: Prune after harvest so light and wind reach inside the crown. Hoppers thrive in shaded, humid trees.
Induce all trees in a block at the same time, so the flowering window is short and hoppers cannot move from early to late trees.
Count hoppers every week from bud swell until the fruits are pea sized, instead of spraying by the calendar.
If a spray is needed, give it before the flowers open. Sprays at full bloom kill the bees and flies that set the fruit.
Do not bring nursery plants carrying hoppers or eggs into a clean orchard.
Wash or wipe sooty mold off small trees and keep weeds low under the canopy to dry the air.
bio: Spiders, lady beetles, lacewing larvae and small wasps eat hoppers and their eggs. Every needless spray kills them.
Beauveria bassiana or Metarhizium anisopliae in an oil based spray can cut hopper numbers in humid weather.
pests.threshold: Start a week after flower induction, when the buds swell: on 5 to 10 trees, tap or shake 10 flowering branches each and count the adults that fly off. Act when the count reaches 4 to 5 adults per flower branch while the fruits are still small, and spray before the flowers open.
pests.rotate: Hoppers in mango areas that get one group spray after spray stop dying, and pyrethroids and neonicotinoids are the groups most overused in Asia. Rotate pymetrozine (9B), buprofezin (16), cartap (14), a neonicotinoid (4A) and a pyrethroid (3A), and never use one group twice in a row in the same flowering.

pests.name: Mango pulp weevil
pests.hint: Tunnels in the pulp darken the flesh after the grub feeds.
pests.no: No spray is recommended. Quarantine, orchard sanitation and irradiation of export fruit control it.
prevent: Do not carry mango plants, fruits, seeds or scions out of the Palawan island group.
Buy planting material only from accredited nurseries outside infested areas.
Pick up and destroy fallen and damaged fruits every few days, so grubs and new adults cannot escape to the soil.
Clear litter and loose bark under and on the trees in the off season, where adults hide until the next flowering.
Export fruit from Palawan goes through the approved irradiation treatment.
pests.threshold: At harvest, cut open 20 fruits per tree in suspect orchards and look for tunnels and grubs in the flesh. Inside Palawan, a find means stricter sanitation. Outside Palawan, any grub is a quarantine case to report at once to the plant quarantine office.

pests.name: Mango cecid fly (kurikong)
pests.local: Farmers call the scab like spots on the fruit kurikong, and other names in use are buti, armalite and saksak walis.
pests.hint: Circular brown to black scab like spots are scattered over the fruit skin.

mango: Moves into the young fruit skin where the larvae feed and spares most natural enemies. Start at day 30 to 35.
Moves into the young fruit skin where the larvae feed and spares most natural enemies. Start at day 30 to 35.
Works on the egg laying flies, but the broad pyrethroid half also kills the wasps that attack the larvae.
Soaks into the skin and reaches young larvae. Toxic to bees and fish, so do not spray open flowers.
Old broad carbamate, toxic to people, bees and fish. A last resort with the full waiting time.

prevent: Write down the flower induction date. The fly starts on young fruit at about day 32 to 35, so plan checks and any spray around it.
Bag the fruits once they are big enough to hold a bag, about 45 to 55 days after induction, to keep the egg laying females off.
Gather and bury fallen fruits and spotted leaves. The larvae leave the spots and drop to the soil to pupate.
Mulch or turn the soil under the canopy during fruiting so fewer larvae can pupate there.
Prune crowded branches after every harvest so the crown dries fast and any spray reaches the fruit.
Induce flowers together with your neighbors. An area that fruits at one time leaves the fly no young fruit later.
bio: Tiny parasitic wasps attack the larvae inside the spots. Weekly broad sprays wipe them out.
Ants, spiders and ground beetles take larvae as they drop to the soil, so leave the litter under the trees unsprayed.
pests.threshold: Mark the flower induction date. From day 30, check 20 young fruits and the new leaves on 5 to 10 trees each week. The attack runs from about day 32 to day 70. Act at the first fresh raised spots on young fruit, because once the scab turns dark the larva has already left.
pests.rotate: Sprays given week after week with the same product breed flies that survive it. Rotate a diamide (28), abamectin (6) and a neonicotinoid or pyrethroid mix (4A, 3A) between sprays, and add a sticker so the spray stays on the fruit.

pests.name: Cacao pod borer
pests.hint: Pods ripen early and turn yellow unevenly.
pests.no: Insecticides are not advised for small farms. The steps on its page work better.

cacao: Only after sleeving and weekly harvest fail. Spray the underside of lower branches where moths rest. Kills weaver ants.
Old broad spray. Kills bees, ants and spiders that guard the pods, and can bring mealybugs after it.
Only after sleeving and weekly harvest fail. Spray the underside of lower branches where moths rest. Kills weaver ants.

prevent: Harvest every 7 days and take every ripening pod, so the larvae have no time to leave and pupate.
Bury the pod husks right after opening, or cover the heap tightly with plastic for 2 weeks so the larvae inside die.
Sleeve young pods, about 8 to 10 cm long, in plastic bags open at the bottom. The moth cannot lay eggs on them.
Prune twice a year to keep trees about 3 meters tall and open, so pods are easy to reach and moths find less shade to rest.
In the lean season strip off all pods once to break the moth's cycle, and keep the same schedule as your neighbors.
bio: Weaver ants (hantik) and black cocoa ants guard the pods against the moth. Keep their nests and keep sprays off them.
Spiders and tiny egg wasps kill the eggs laid on the pod surface.
Beauveria bassiana sprayed on the lower branches where moths rest can kill some adults.
pests.threshold: At every harvest round, split 20 ripe pods per block and count those with clumped, stuck beans or small exit holes. If many are hit, harvest every 7 days and start sleeving the young pods. Spray only the moth resting sites if that still fails.

pests.name: Coffee berry borer
pests.hint: A small round entry hole shows on the berry, with brown frass over it.

coffee: Must go on while females are still in the hole, before they reach the bean. Kills bees and natural enemies.
Old, toxic organophosphate. A last resort only, with the full waiting time before harvest.

avoid: Copper hydroxide
A copper fungicide for leaf rust and berry disease. It does nothing to the berry borer.
Bordeaux mixture
A copper fungicide for leaf rust and berry disease. It does nothing to the berry borer.
prevent: Pick ripe berries every 2 to 3 weeks through the season, and do not leave over ripe berries on the tree.
Gather fallen and black berries from the ground and destroy them. Borers wait in them for the next crop.
After the main harvest, strip every berry left on the tree, green, ripe or dry, to break the borer's cycle.
Dry harvested beans fast and well, and store them in sealed sacks, so borers in them die and cannot fly back.
Hang lure traps with a methanol and ethanol mix when few berries are on the trees. About 4 traps per 50 trees caught the most in one highland trial.
Prune and fertilize on time. Open, healthy trees are easier to pick clean and dry faster.
bio: Spray Beauveria bassiana early in the season when females are boring in. It kills many in humid places, fewer in dry ones.
Small parasitic wasps attack the borer inside the berry. They help a little where they are present.
pests.threshold: From about 3 months after flowering, take 5 green berries from each of 20 trees across the block every 2 weeks. Act when more than 2 percent carry fresh holes and the females are still in the hole. Once they are inside the bean, a spray does little.
pests.rotate: The berry borer once resisted endosulfan in New Caledonia after years of one product. With few registered choices here, keep sprays rare and let picking and sanitation do the work.

pests.name: Corn leaf aphid
pests.hint: Blue green aphids crowd the whorl and the tassel, which turn sticky and then black with sooty mold.

sources.label: DA Caraga Corn Program, Mga Dangan sa Mais (Technoguide 01, 2020)

corn_yellow: Stops aphid feeding and spares lady beetles, hover flies and the tiny wasps that eat aphids.
A seed treatment: it guards the first weeks, while the aphid mostly builds up later, at tasseling.
Kills the lady beetles and wasps that end aphid outbreaks, so aphids often bounce back. Last resort.
The pyrethroid part kills the lady beetles and wasps that end aphid outbreaks. A last resort.
Old and broad: it kills the natural enemies that usually end aphid outbreaks.
Old and broad: it kills the natural enemies that usually end aphid outbreaks.
Weak on aphids and very toxic to bees, fish and shrimp. It is a borer granule first.
corn_sweet: Stops aphid feeding and spares lady beetles, hover flies and the tiny wasps that eat aphids.
A seed treatment: it guards the first weeks, while the aphid mostly builds up later, at tasseling.
Kills the lady beetles and wasps that end aphid outbreaks, so aphids often bounce back. Last resort.
The pyrethroid part kills the lady beetles and wasps that end aphid outbreaks. A last resort.
Old and broad: it kills the natural enemies that usually end aphid outbreaks.
Old and broad: it kills the natural enemies that usually end aphid outbreaks.
Weak on aphids and very toxic to bees, fish and shrimp. It is a borer granule first.
corn_glutinous: Stops aphid feeding and spares lady beetles, hover flies and the tiny wasps that eat aphids.
A seed treatment: it guards the first weeks, while the aphid mostly builds up later, at tasseling.
Kills the lady beetles and wasps that end aphid outbreaks, so aphids often bounce back. Last resort.
The pyrethroid part kills the lady beetles and wasps that end aphid outbreaks. A last resort.
Old and broad: it kills the natural enemies that usually end aphid outbreaks.
Old and broad: it kills the natural enemies that usually end aphid outbreaks.
Weak on aphids and very toxic to bees, fish and shrimp. It is a borer granule first.

avoid: Buprofezin
A growth regulator for hoppers and whiteflies. Aphids barely respond to it.
prevent: Plant on time and water in dry spells: drought stressed corn suffers most from aphids.
Keep itch grass, Johnson grass and other grassy weeds off the borders. They host the aphid between crops.
Feed balanced nitrogen, since heavy urea makes soft growth that aphids crowd on.
Pull out plants with mosaic streaks early, because this aphid also spreads mosaic viruses.
bio: Lady beetles, hover fly larvae, lacewings and tiny parasitic wasps often wipe out colonies on their own. Spare them.
Heavy rain also knocks colonies down, so watch a few days before you spray.
Beauveria or Lecanicillium fungus infects aphids in humid weather.
pests.threshold: From late whorl to tasseling, check 20 plants at each of five spots each week. Act only when more than half the plants carry colonies of 100 or more aphids on the whorl or tassel before pollen shed, mostly in a dry spell. After pollen shed a spray rarely pays.

pests.name: Corn seedling maggot
pests.hint: The center leaf of a young seedling yellows and dies, with a cream colored maggot boring down inside the shoot.

sources.label: DA Caraga Corn Program, Mga Dangan sa Mais (Technoguide 01, 2020)

corn_yellow: A seed treatment: it guards the seedling through the first two to three weeks, when the maggot strikes.
A seed treatment: it guards the seedling through the first two to three weeks, when the maggot strikes.
A seed treatment of two group 4A parts: it guards the first two to three weeks.
Very toxic to fish, shrimp and bees: use it on seed or in the furrow, far from ponds.
Sold as a seed treatment that also guards against cutworm and white grub in the first weeks.
A spray hits only the flies and eggs, not the maggot inside the shoot, and kills early natural enemies.
Old and broad: it kills the spiders and wasps the field needs later against borers.
Highly toxic to people, birds and fish. Granules in the furrow only, as a last resort.
A spray hits only the flies and eggs, not the maggot inside the shoot. Seed treatment works better.
Old carbamate, very toxic. The neonicotinoid seed treatments do the same job more safely.
corn_sweet: A seed treatment: it guards the seedling through the first two to three weeks, when the maggot strikes.
A seed treatment: it guards the seedling through the first two to three weeks, when the maggot strikes.
A seed treatment of two group 4A parts: it guards the first two to three weeks.
Very toxic to fish, shrimp and bees: use it on seed or in the furrow, far from ponds.
Sold as a seed treatment that also guards against cutworm and white grub in the first weeks.
A spray hits only the flies and eggs, not the maggot inside the shoot, and kills early natural enemies.
Old and broad: it kills the spiders and wasps the field needs later against borers.
Highly toxic to people, birds and fish. Granules in the furrow only, as a last resort.
A spray hits only the flies and eggs, not the maggot inside the shoot. Seed treatment works better.
Old carbamate, very toxic. The neonicotinoid seed treatments do the same job more safely.
corn_glutinous: A seed treatment: it guards the seedling through the first two to three weeks, when the maggot strikes.
A seed treatment: it guards the seedling through the first two to three weeks, when the maggot strikes.
A seed treatment of two group 4A parts: it guards the first two to three weeks.
Very toxic to fish, shrimp and bees: use it on seed or in the furrow, far from ponds.
Sold as a seed treatment that also guards against cutworm and white grub in the first weeks.
A spray hits only the flies and eggs, not the maggot inside the shoot, and kills early natural enemies.
Old and broad: it kills the spiders and wasps the field needs later against borers.
Highly toxic to people, birds and fish. Granules in the furrow only, as a last resort.
A spray hits only the flies and eggs, not the maggot inside the shoot. Seed treatment works better.
Old carbamate, very toxic. The neonicotinoid seed treatments do the same job more safely.

prevent: Plant treated seed: the seed treatment covers the first two weeks, when the fly lays its eggs.
Plant at the same time as the farms around you, and do not plant late beside young corn that is already attacked.
Prepare a fine, well drained seedbed and plant at the right depth, so seedlings race through the risky first two weeks.
Pull and destroy seedlings with dead hearts early, and replant the gaps.
Plow under stubble and clear grassy weeds that host the fly between crops.
bio: Spiders, ants, rove beetles and small wasps attack the eggs and maggots. Avoid broad sprays at emergence.
pests.threshold: From emergence to day 14, check 20 seedlings at each of five spots every two or three days for tiny white eggs on the leaves and yellowing center leaves. Once a dead heart shows, the maggot is inside and a spray comes too late. Where many seedlings carry eggs in the first week and the seed was not treated, a spray on the young plants can still pay.

pests.name: Sugarcane aphid (yellow sorghum aphid)
pests.hint: Pale yellow to gray aphids pack the underside of the lower leaves, which turn shiny with honeydew and then black with sooty mold.

sources.label: ICRISAT, Sugarcane aphid resistance in sorghum

prevent: Plant early and at the same time as nearby fields. Late sorghum gets hit hardest.
Use treated seed and a tolerant sorghum hybrid where one is sold.
Do not spray pyrethroids or organophosphates for other pests: they kill the lady beetles and set off aphid outbreaks.
Remove Johnson grass, volunteer sorghum and old ratoon cane that carry the aphid between crops.
Water in dry spells, since stressed plants suffer most.
bio: Lady beetles, hover fly larvae, lacewings and small parasitic wasps often hold colonies down. Spare them.
Beauveria or Lecanicillium fungus infects aphids in humid weather.
pests.threshold: From the boot stage, check the underside of the lower and middle leaves on 20 plants at each of five spots every week. The usual rule is to act when about one plant in four carries colonies of 50 or more aphids with honeydew showing. In cane, watch young fields in dry spells, when colonies spread fastest.

pests.name: Sorghum shoot fly
pests.hint: Seedlings one to four weeks old show dead hearts, where the center leaf dries and pulls out easily while the outer leaves stay green.

sources.label: Indian Journal of Entomology, Sorghum shoot fly and seed treatment

prevent: Plant early in the season and all at once with nearby fields: late sorghum gets the most shoot fly.
Use treated seed, sow a little extra, and thin out the seedlings with dead hearts.
Choose glossy leaved, tolerant varieties where sold. The fly lays fewer eggs on them.
Set fishmeal bait traps around young fields to catch the flies.
Pull and destroy dead hearts, and clear volunteer sorghum and grassy weeds that carry the fly between crops.
bio: Egg wasps, spiders and ants kill many eggs and maggots. Avoid broad sprays at emergence.
pests.threshold: From 7 to 30 days after emergence, check 20 seedlings at each of five spots twice a week for small white eggs under the leaves and for dead hearts. Once a dead heart shows the maggot is inside and a spray comes too late, so the real decision is treated seed and an early planting date.

prevent: Sow clean seed from a crop free of mosaic. Aphids carry the virus from plant to plant.
Go easy on nitrogen. Soft, lush growth feeds aphids.
Remove weeds and volunteer legumes around the field before planting.
Pinch off and crush the first colonies on the shoot tips, or wash them off with water.
Rows of corn around or between bean rows block many winged aphids coming in.
bio: Lady beetles, syrphid fly larvae, lacewings and small wasps eat or parasitize the aphids. Leave them unsprayed.
Ants guard aphid colonies from their enemies. Keep ants off the plants and destroy nests near the field.
Soap, oil and neem sprays kill aphids on contact with little harm to most helpers.
pests.threshold: Twice a week look at the shoot tips, flowers and young pods of 20 plants at 5 spots. Act when colonies sit on more than 1 in 5 plants before flowering and you see few lady beetles, syrphid larvae or parasitized aphids. Act sooner on young plants, since aphids spread bean mosaic virus.

pests.name: Pod sucking bugs
pests.sci: Nezara viridula, Riptortus linearis, Clavigralla gibbosa
pests.hint: Green stink bugs or slender brown bugs suck the young pods, leaving dark spots, shriveled seeds and pods that drop early.

sources.label: ATI and DA RFO 02, Sitao Production Guide

soybean: Kills bees at flowering. Spray late in the day, at pod fill, and only when counts pass the threshold.
Old broad spray, hard on bees, fish and the bugs' enemies. A last resort.
An old carbamate. It kills bugs on contact but is hard on their egg wasps.
mungbean: Kills bees at flowering. Spray late in the day, at pod fill, and only when counts pass the threshold.

prevent: Plant on the same dates as your neighbors. Late fields draw the bugs from early ones.
Sow a small strip of the same crop a little earlier as a trap. Handpick or spray only that strip.
Crush egg rafts and the clusters of young nymphs under the leaves.
Remove legume weeds and volunteer plants around the field.
Harvest pods on time. Dry pods left in the field feed the next generation.
bio: Egg wasps such as Trissolcus and Telenomus, tachinid flies, spiders and ants attack the eggs and nymphs. Fewer broad sprays leave more of them.
pests.threshold: From pod set, shake the plants over a cloth along 1 meter of row at 5 spots, early in the morning. Act when you count about 2 bugs (adults and big nymphs) per meter of row during pod filling.

pests.name: Bean weevil (bruchid)
pests.hint: Stored seeds show round exit holes, small brown beetles and tiny white eggs glued on the seed coat.
pests.no: Do not spray seed you will eat or sell. Dry the seed well and keep it in sealed, airtight containers so the weevils die.

sources.label: Bulletin of Entomological Research, Hermetic bags against Callosobruchus in stored mung bean

prevent: Harvest pods as soon as they dry. Weevils lay eggs on pods left long in the field.
Sun dry the seed well before storing, until it cracks when bitten.
Store in airtight containers such as sealed drums, thick plastic bags inside sacks, or bottles filled to the top. The weevils die without air.
Mix stored seed you will eat with a thin coat of cooking oil, or with fine sand or wood ash, so eggs cannot hatch.
Clean the store and old sacks before the new harvest goes in, and never mix new seed with old infested seed.
pests.threshold: Check stored seed every 2 weeks: small round exit holes or white eggs stuck on the seed mean the weevils are breeding. Act at once, since numbers double fast in warm stores.

pests.name: Bean leaf roller
pests.hint: Leaves are folded or webbed together and eaten from inside, leaving a silvery, papery look.

sources.label: Peanut CRSP Philippines, Peanut production guide (M. K. Palomar, editor)

prevent: Pick and crush rolled leaves with larvae inside while the attack is light.
Remove legume weeds around the field, and avoid legume after legume in the same plot.
Plow under crop remains after harvest to destroy pupae.
Plant on the same dates as your neighbors so the moths do not move from field to field.
bio: Small wasps, spiders and predatory bugs kill many larvae in the rolls. Leave light attacks unsprayed.
Bt sprayed on young larvae, before the leaves are fully rolled, spares these helpers.
pests.threshold: Check 20 plants at 5 spots weekly from 2 weeks after emergence. Act only when more than 1 in 4 leaves are rolled with live larvae before flowering. Plants make up for light leaf loss.

pests.name: Groundnut leafminer
pests.hint: Small brown blotches appear on the leaflets where tiny green caterpillars mine inside, then fold the leaflets together.

sources.label: Peanut CRSP Philippines, Peanut production guide (M. K. Palomar, editor)

peanut: Old broad spray with a short hold on larvae inside leaves. A last resort.
Two old broad chemicals in one. Very hard on bees and fish.
soybean: Kills the miner's wasps and bees at flowering. Spray only when counts pass the threshold.
Old broad spray, hard on bees and on the miner's wasps. A last resort.
Old broad spray with a short hold on larvae inside leaves. A last resort.
Two old broad chemicals in one. Very hard on bees and fish.
Very toxic to bees and can bring mites back. A last resort.
Kills the miner's wasps and bees at flowering. Spray only when counts pass the threshold.

prevent: Plant early in the wet season. The miner builds up fast in dry weather.
Water during dry spells where you can. Stressed plants suffer most.
Rotate with crops outside the bean family and remove legume weeds around the field.
Intercropping peanut with corn or pearl millet cuts miner numbers.
Plow under crop remains after harvest to destroy pupae.
bio: Many small wasps parasitize the larvae in the mines. Broad sprays kill them first.
pests.threshold: Weekly from 3 weeks after emergence, check 20 plants at 5 spots for mined or webbed leaflets with live larvae. Act when more than 1 in 4 leaflets is damaged before pod filling, mostly in dry spells.

pests.name: Southern green stink bug
pests.hint: Green shield shaped bugs that smell when touched suck the young pods, which turn warty, bent or fall.
pests.no: No product names this bug on okra or tomato labels yet. Handpick the bugs in the cool morning, crush the egg rafts, keep weeds down and rotate crops.

sources.label: DA RFO 02, Okra Production Guide

prevent: Handpick the bugs in the cool morning, when they are slow, and drop them in soapy water.
Crush egg rafts and the clusters of young nymphs under the leaves.
Keep weeds and legume volunteers down around the field.
Rotate okra and tomato with crops the bug likes less, such as leafy greens.
A strip of an early sown legume or sesbania nearby draws the bugs away. Clear it once they gather.
bio: Egg wasps such as Trissolcus basalis, tachinid flies, spiders and ants attack the eggs and nymphs.
pests.threshold: Twice a week check 20 plants for bugs and the raft shaped egg masses under the leaves. Act when you find more than 1 bug in every 5 plants on okra pods or green tomatoes.

pests.name: Hornworms (sweet potato and taro)
pests.sci: Agrius convolvuli (sweet potato, kangkong), Hippotion celerio (taro)
pests.hint: Big green or brown caterpillars with a horn on the tail eat whole leaves, leaving bare stalks and large droppings below.

sources.label: Pacific Pests, Pathogens and Weeds: Sweetpotato hornworm
Pacific Pests, Pathogens and Weeds: Taro hornworm

prevent: Handpick the larvae in the morning or evening. Follow the fresh droppings to find them.
Plow after harvest to turn up the pupae in the soil for birds and the sun.
Keep wild morning glory and other vine weeds of the same family away from sweet potato and kangkong.
Do not plant a new field right beside an old one full of larvae.
bio: Small wasps and tachinid flies parasitize the larvae. Leave larvae with white cocoons on their backs alive.
Birds, chickens and ducks pick off many larvae and pupae.
pests.threshold: Walk the field weekly and look for big droppings and stripped vines. Handpick every larva you find. Spray Bt only when young larvae average more than 1 per plant over a whole patch.

pests.name: Yam and rhizome scale
pests.hint: Tubers and rhizomes, most often in storage, are crusted with tiny round gray to brown scales, then shrivel and sprout poorly.
pests.no: Field sprays do not reach them. Keep only clean seed tubers and rhizomes, discard crusted ones, and store them dry and airy.

sources.label: PROSEA: Dioscorea alata (purple yam)
Vikaspedia: pests and diseases management in ginger

prevent: Plant only clean seed tubers and rhizomes. Throw out or burn any piece with a crust of scales.
Store seed pieces dry, airy and shaded, on racks or slatted shelves, not in heaps on a damp floor.
Do not plant ginger, turmeric or ubi after one another in the same field.
Clean the store and old sacks before the new harvest goes in.
bio: Small wasps and lady beetles feed on the scales. They work best where stores and fields are not sprayed.
pests.threshold: Check every seed rhizome and tuber at harvest and before planting. Any piece with grey or white crusts should not be planted.

pests.name: Sweet potato leaf folder
pests.hint: Leaves are folded and tied with silk, and small caterpillars inside eat windows in the leaf until it turns brown.

sources.label: Pacific Pests, Pathogens and Weeds: Sweetpotato leaf folder
FAO AGRIS: Biology of the black and green leaf folders of sweet potato (Philippines)

prevent: Pick and crush folded leaves with larvae inside while the attack is light.
Remove wild morning glory and other vine weeds of the same family around the field.
Plant clean vine tips and keep the crop growing fast with enough water.
Rotate with rice or corn, and do not plant beside an old infested field.
bio: Small wasps, spiders and predatory bugs kill many larvae in the folds. Leave light attacks unsprayed.
pests.threshold: Check 20 plants at 5 spots weekly in the first 2 months. Act only when more than 1 in 4 leaves are folded with live larvae. The vines regrow from light damage.

pests.name: Ginger and turmeric shoot borer
pests.hint: Caterpillars bore into the leafy stem, leaving a hole with frass, and the center shoot yellows and dries.

sources.label: Vikaspedia: pests and diseases management in ginger

prevent: Each week in the rainy months, cut out shoots with a dry, yellow center and a bore hole, and destroy the larva inside.
Plant clean, borer free seed rhizomes.
Keep castor and other host plants of the borer away from ginger and turmeric fields.
After harvest, collect and burn old stems and leaves.
bio: Egg wasps and small larval wasps attack the borer. Bt on young shoots reaches newly hatched larvae.
pests.threshold: In the rainy months, check the clumps weekly for yellow, dried center shoots with a bore hole and frass. Act when more than 1 in 10 clumps shows fresh damage after you have cut out the dead shoots.

pests.name: Ginger leaf roller
pests.hint: Green caterpillars with a black head fold the leaves lengthwise and feed hidden inside the rolls, and heavy attacks strip the leaves.

sources.label: TNAU Agritech Portal, Insect pests of turmeric and ginger
Kerala Agricultural University, Turmeric leaf roller

avoid: Dimethoate
Made for sucking insects. Weak on caterpillars hidden in rolled leaves.
prevent: Pick off and crush rolled leaves with the larva inside.
Keep weeds down around the beds and remove old leaves after harvest.
Do not plant ginger or turmeric after one another in the same field.
bio: Small wasps and spiders kill many larvae. Leave light attacks unsprayed.
pests.threshold: Check the clumps weekly. Pick off rolled leaves by hand. Spray only when more than 1 in 4 leaves are rolled with live larvae.

pests.name: Sweet potato weevil
pests.hint: Roots have small feeding holes and dark tunnels inside, smell bad and taste bitter, and the vine base is cracked and swollen.
pests.no: Sprays do little: the grubs live inside vines and roots. Clean cuttings, hilling, closing soil cracks and harvest on time are the control.

sources.label: DA RFO 2 Sweet Potato Production Guide
UPLB Philippine Agricultural Scientist: managing sweet potato weevil

avoid: Fenthion
Leaf sprays do not reach weevil grubs inside the vines and roots. Clean cuttings and hilling work better.
Cyfluthrin
No label names it for this weevil, and a leaf spray does not reach the grubs inside the roots.
prevent: Plant clean vine tips cut from the top of healthy vines, not old stems that may hide eggs and grubs.
Hill up soil around the plants and close soil cracks, so the weevils cannot reach the roots. Water in dry spells.
Harvest on time. Roots left long in the ground take more damage.
Rotate with rice or corn, and remove volunteer sweet potato and wild morning glory weeds.
Destroy crop remains and damaged roots right after harvest, and never plant beside an old field.
Sex pheromone traps catch many males and show when the weevils arrive.
bio: Beauveria bassiana or Metarhizium anisopliae on the soil and in pheromone traps infect the weevils.
Ants and earwigs eat weevil eggs and grubs in the soil.
pests.threshold: Hang sex pheromone traps from planting and read them weekly. A rising catch means weevils are moving in. Check soil cracks over the roots in dry spells and dig a few plants each month from root set.

pests.name: Cassava white scale
pests.hint: Stems are crusted with tiny white scales, leaves yellow and drop, and cuttings taken from these stems sprout poorly.
pests.no: Field sprays rarely pay. Plant clean cuttings, burn crusted stems, and keep the field and its edges free of old stalks.

sources.label: DA Bicol: UPLB study on cassava pests

prevent: Cut planting stakes only from clean, scale free stems.
Burn crusted stems instead of leaving them in or near the field.
Keep the field and its edges free of old cassava stalks.
Plant soon after cutting the stakes. Stakes stored long in dry heat suffer more.
Do not plant cassava after cassava in a field that had heavy scale.
bio: Lady beetles and small wasps feed on the scales. Unsprayed fields keep more of them.
pests.threshold: Check stems before cutting planting stakes. Any stem with white crusts should not be used. In the field, act on the first crusted stems by cutting and burning them.

pests.name: Potato tuber moth
pests.hint: Small caterpillars mine the leaves and stems, then tunnel into tubers near the surface and in storage, leaving holes with dark droppings.

sources.label: Pacific Pests, Pathogens and Weeds: Potato tuber moth
International Potato Center: potato pests and diseases

potato: Works on larvae mining the leaves and stems. It cannot reach larvae already inside the tubers.
Old broad spray that kills the wasps of this moth and of the leafminer. A last resort.
Banned in many countries. Very toxic to fish and bees. A last resort.
Kills the wasps that hold this moth and the leafminer down in potato. A last resort.

prevent: Plant clean, whole seed tubers. Never plant tubers with tunnels.
Hill up well so tubers stay at least 5 cm under the soil, and water in dry spells so the soil does not crack.
Harvest soon after the vines die, and never leave dug tubers in the field overnight.
Store seed tubers in a clean, screened store, covered with dry leaves of lantana or eucalyptus to keep moths off.
Destroy cull tubers and volunteer potato plants, and rotate away from potato, tomato and eggplant.
bio: Bt powder dusted on stored seed tubers protects them for months.
Small wasps attack the larvae in leaves and tubers. Spare them by spraying less in the field.
pests.threshold: Hang sex pheromone traps in the field and in the store, and read them weekly. Act when catches climb and mined leaves show on more than 1 in 10 plants. Near harvest, protect tubers by hilling rather than spraying.

pests.name: Yam leaf beetle
pests.sci: Lilioceris livida (Crioceris livida), Galerucida bicolor and related leaf beetles
pests.hint: Beetles and their grubs chew holes in the leaves and eat the vine tips, and heavy attacks leave the vines bare.
pests.no: No product names this beetle on its label. Pick off beetles and grubs by hand while the vines are young, and keep the field free of weeds.

sources.label: Korada and others, Insect pests and their management in yam production and storage (review)

prevent: Pick off beetles and grubs by hand while the vines are young, and crush the egg clusters under the leaves.
Keep the field and its edges free of weeds and wild yam vines.
Remove and burn old vines after harvest, where beetles shelter.
Do not plant ubi after ubi in the same field.
bio: Spiders, ants, assassin bugs and birds eat the grubs. Leave them unsprayed.
pests.threshold: Check the young vines twice a week for beetles and for grubs hidden under their own wet droppings. Pick them off whenever you see them. The vines are most at risk in the first 2 months.

pests.name: Aphids
pests.sci: Myzus persicae, Aphis gossypii, Lipaphis erysimi, Brevicoryne brassicae
pests.hint: Clusters of small soft green, gray or black insects suck under young leaves, which curl, turn sticky and grow black sooty mold.

prevent: Plant nectar plants such as Turnera, Cassia cobanensis or cadena de amor along roads and borders to feed the parasitic wasps.
Prune and burn heavily eaten fronds or leaves early, before the larvae spin cocoons.
Collect the cocoons from leaf bases and from the soil around the trunk, and loosen that soil to expose them.
Avoid broad spectrum sprays: they kill the parasites and set off new outbreaks.
Wear gloves and long sleeves when you work among them, because the spines sting.
bio: Parasitic wasps and flies, assassin bugs and a virus disease usually end outbreaks. Protect them.
Bt sprays on young larvae work well and spare these natural enemies.
Light traps at night catch the moths before they lay eggs.
pests.threshold: In oil palm, count live larvae on one lower frond of sample palms every month. The usual action level is about 5 to 10 larvae per frond, or fresh damage spreading across patches. In abaca, banana and coconut, act when young larvae spread over many plants. Outbreaks often crash on their own from disease.

pests.name: Pink bollworm
pests.hint: Flowers stay closed like rosettes, and small pink caterpillars inside the green bolls eat the seeds and stain the lint.

sources.label: PhilFIDA, Technoguide on Cotton Pests and their Management

prevent: Keep a cotton free break of a few months between seasons, and pull and destroy all stalks right after the last picking.
Plant short season varieties at the same time as your neighbors, and never keep a ratoon crop.
Pick off and destroy rosette flowers and fallen bolls during the season.
Dry the planting seed well in the sun and store it sealed, since resting larvae hide inside seed.
Pheromone ropes that confuse the moths cut mating when many farms use them together.
Clean up okra and wild mallows near the field after harvest. They keep the moth going.
bio: Trichogramma egg wasps, lacewings and small predatory bugs take eggs and young larvae. Spare them by spraying only on counts.
pests.threshold: From flowering, look for rosette flowers and open 20 green bolls a week from several spots. Act when about 1 boll in 10 holds larvae, or when sex pheromone traps catch 8 or more moths a night for three nights in a row.

pests.name: Cotton stainer
pests.hint: Red and black bugs feed on the bolls, young bolls shrivel, and the lint comes out stained.

sources.label: PhilFIDA, Technoguide on Cotton Pests and their Management
DA RFO 02, Okra Production Guide

cotton: Old broad organophosphate: aim it at the bug clusters on open bolls and keep it off flowers where bees work.

prevent: Pick open bolls promptly, and remove the fallen, rotting bolls where the bugs gather and breed.
Clear kapok, wild mallows and other host plants from around the field.
Put out small heaps of cotton seed as bait, then shake the bugs gathered there into a pail of soapy water.
In the cool morning, when the bugs are slow, shake the plants over a pail of soapy water.
Plow under the crop debris after harvest and keep a break before the next cotton.
bio: Assassin bugs, spiders, birds and ants prey on stainers. Spare them.
A larger red predator bug that looks like the stainer feeds on it. Do not kill it by mistake.
pests.threshold: From the first open bolls, check 20 plants at each of five spots every week. Act when clusters of bugs feed on many open or nearly open bolls. A few bugs on fallen bolls do little harm.

pests.name: Bagworms
pests.sci: Metisa plana, Pteroma pendula, Mahasena corbetti
pests.hint: Small cases made of chewed leaf bits hang under the fronds, and the leaves turn gray and ragged as if scorched.

sources.label: MPOB, Bt sprays against bagworm outbreaks in oil palm

prevent: Plant nectar plants such as Turnera, Cassia cobanensis or cadena de amor along roads and borders to feed the parasitic wasps.
Cut and burn badly infested lower fronds early, while the outbreak is still small.
Avoid broad spectrum sprays: they kill the parasitoids, and bigger outbreaks follow.
Check seedlings and planting material for cases before bringing them in.
bio: Parasitic wasps and assassin bugs are the main enemies of bagworms. Protect them.
Bt on young larvae spares these natural enemies.
pests.threshold: Count live larvae on one lower frond of sample palms every month. The usual oil palm action level is 10 live larvae per frond. Treat when most larvae are young, as a new generation hatches.

pests.name: Sugarcane stem borers
pests.sci: Chilo infuscatellus, Tetramoera schistaceana, Chilo sacchariphagus
pests.hint: Young shoots show dead hearts, and older canes have bore holes, tunnels and frass at the nodes.

sources.label: UPLB, Recommendations for the management of major arthropod pests of sugarcane and corn

sugarcane: Spray or drench young cane while larvae are in the shoots. Once they are deep in the stalk it reaches few.
Group 28 like chlorantraniliprole: do not rotate it with another 28.
Highly toxic to people, birds and fish: furrow granules only, as a last resort.

prevent: Plant healthy setts from fields with few borers, and throw out any sett with a bore hole.
Hill up young cane and keep the soil moist in the first months: the early shoot borer favors dry, loose soil.
Cut out dead hearts at ground level, with the larva inside, and destroy them as you find them.
Strip dry lower leaves, remove late water shoots, and do not overfeed nitrogen.
Plant tolerant varieties, cut low at harvest, and do not leave mature cane standing late.
bio: Release Trichogramma chilonis egg wasp cards at regular intervals from the first month while the moths are flying.
A small larval wasp, Cotesia flavipes, plus earwigs and ants kill many larvae and eggs. Avoid broad sprays.
pests.threshold: From one to four months after planting, count dead hearts in 10 meters of row at five spots every two weeks, and at harvest split 20 canes to count bored joints. Act while dead hearts are still appearing in young cane. Once canes are tall, rely on egg wasp releases rather than sprays.

pests.name: Red striped soft scale (RSSI)
pests.hint: Small flat scales with reddish stripes and white cottony egg sacs crowd the leaves, which turn sticky, black with sooty mold, then dry.

sources.label: Philstar, SRA steps up fight vs sugarcane pests (2026)
Negros Now Daily, SRA intensifies campaign vs RSSI infestation

sugarcane: Highly toxic: granules may slow the scale from inside the cane, but they kill birds and fish. Last resort only.

prevent: Take setts only from fields free of the scale, strip their leaves before moving them, and never bring cane points from infested areas.
Strip and burn infested lower leaves as soon as patches show, then clean knives, carts and boots.
Do not move trash, cane tops or planting material out of an infested farm.
Check fields near infested areas every two weeks, above all in dry months.
Clean old trash out of infested fields before the ratoon regrows.
bio: A small aphelinid wasp already parasitizes this scale in local fields, 30 to 67 percent in surveys. Avoid broad sprays that kill it.
White, pink and black fungi grow on dying scales in wet weather. Beauveria, Metarhizium or Lecanicillium sprays help in humid months.
Lady beetles feed on the crawlers.
pests.threshold: Every two weeks, check the lower leaves of 20 stools at each of five spots, starting at the field edges, and look harder in dry months. Strip and burn the first patches at once. A spray pays only where scales crowd many leaves and fresh white egg sacs show that crawlers are coming out.

pests.name: Sugarcane woolly aphid
pests.hint: White woolly patches of aphids cover the underside of the leaves, and the leaves below turn black with sooty mold and dry from the tip.

sources.label: Pacific Pests, Pathogens, Weeds and Pesticides, Sugarcane woolly aphid

prevent: Plant clean setts with the leaves stripped off, and do not bring planting material from infested farms.
Feed balanced nitrogen: heavy urea makes soft, lush cane that the aphid favors.
Strip and burn heavily infested lower leaves early.
Keep rows wide enough for air to move, and keep the field weed free.
bio: The larva of the moth Dipha aphidivora and the lacewing Micromus igorotus eat whole colonies. Move them from old patches to new ones.
The tiny wasp Encarsia flavoscutellum parasitizes the aphid. Avoid broad sprays.
Metarhizium or Beauveria fungus sprays work in humid weather.
pests.threshold: In cool, humid months, check the underside of the upper leaves on 20 stools at each of five spots every two weeks. Act on the first colonies by moving predators in or stripping leaves. Field wide sprays rarely reach the colonies and kill the predators that end outbreaks.

pests.name: Pineapple mealybug and mealybug wilt
pests.sci: Dysmicoccus brevipes, with pineapple mealybug wilt associated viruses
pests.hint: Leaf tips turn red, then yellow and pink, curl down and dry, while pink mealybugs hide at the base of the plant and on the roots.

sources.label: DOST PCAARRD, Biocontrol agents against Queen pineapple pests

pineapple: Moves down to the roots and plant base where mealybugs hide. It acts slowly, so treat early.
Very toxic to bees: aim it at the plant base, never on flowering weeds.
Very toxic to bees: aim it at the plant base, never on flowering weeds.
Works on crawlers and young nymphs only, as they molt.
Smothers the mealybugs it touches, but adds little at the roots.
Works on crawlers and young nymphs only. Slow but kind to lady beetles.
Old broad organophosphate: it kills the lady beetles and wasps that eat mealybugs. Last resort.
Old broad organophosphate: it kills the lady beetles and wasps that eat mealybugs. Last resort.
Old broad organophosphate: it kills the lady beetles and wasps that eat mealybugs. Last resort.
Old broad organophosphate: it kills the lady beetles and wasps that eat mealybugs. Last resort.
Old broad organophosphate: it kills the lady beetles and wasps that eat mealybugs. Last resort.

prevent: Plant only clean crowns, slips and suckers, and check their bases before planting.
Control the ants, above all the big headed ant, with a registered ant bait around the blocks. Without ants the mealybugs stay few.
Pull out and destroy wilted plants together with the plants beside them.
Plow out old plants and remove crop residue fully before replanting, with a fallow when you can.
Check field edges first, since spread starts there, and keep weeds and nearby hosts down.
bio: Lady beetles such as Cryptolaemus, lacewings and small parasitic wasps eat mealybugs once the ants are kept away.
Beauveria, Metarhizium and Lecanicillium fungi infect mealybugs in moist weather.
pests.threshold: Every month, check the base and roots of 5 plants at each of ten spots for pink mealybugs and the ants that tend them, and watch field edges for red leaf tips. Act when mealybugs turn up in several spots, and deal with the ants first. Once leaves wilt, that plant will not recover.

pests.name: Bamboo powderpost beetle
pests.hint: Cut culms and poles fill with tiny round holes and pour out fine powder.
ai: Deltamethrin (dip or spray on fresh culms)

sources.label: AGRIS, Prophylactic treatments of newly felled bamboo against powderpost beetle (Laguna and Rizal)

prevent: Cut only mature culms of three years or more, in the dry season, when the starch the beetles feed on is lowest.
Leave cut culms standing upright with branches and leaves on for a few weeks, so the leaves draw the starch out.
Soak fresh culms in running or often changed water for several weeks to wash the starch out.
Smoke or heat treat poles over a fire, or soak them in water with a boron salt, before use.
Store poles dry, off the ground and under a roof, away from old infested bamboo.
pests.threshold: Check stored poles and cut culms every month for small round holes and fine powder. Treat or burn infested poles at once, so the beetles do not spread through the whole pile.

pests.name: Pineapple scale
pests.hint: Tiny round white scales crowd on the leaves and fruit, the leaves show small rusty or yellow spots, and heavy crusts weaken the plant and mar the fruit.
pests.no: No spray for this scale is listed in Philippine guides; plant clean crowns and slips, and pull out and destroy heavily crusted plants.

sources.label: Vikaspedia, Pineapple pests
Naturalis, Diaspis bromeliae

pineapple: Acts slowly but moves through the plant to scales on the leaves and fruit.
Smothers crawlers and young scales it touches. Needs full cover, and never in hot midday sun.
Works on crawlers and young scales only. Time it for when crawlers are out.

prevent: Plant clean crowns and slips: check their bases and leaves, and throw out crusted ones.
Pull out and destroy heavily crusted plants.
Clear old plantings and residue before replanting, since scales carry over on old plants.
Avoid broad insecticides for other pests. They kill the small wasps that hold scales down.
bio: Tiny parasitic wasps and lady beetles attack the scales. Spare them.
pests.threshold: Every month, check the leaves and fruit of 5 plants at each of ten spots, and check crowns and slips before planting. Act when scale crusts spread on the leaves in several spots or show on young fruit, timing the spray for when the crawlers are out.

pests.name: Pineapple red mite
pests.hint: Tiny orange red mites gather at the pale base of the leaves and on the crown and fruit, leaving brown scabby patches where they feed.
pests.no: No spray for this mite is listed in Philippine guides; plant clean slips and crowns, and keep plants watered in dry months when the mite builds up.

sources.label: Vikaspedia, Pineapple pests

pineapple: Mites resist it after repeated use: switch to another group for the next spray.
Slow. Works best on eggs and young mites.
Can burn leaves in hot midday sun. Spray in the cool of the day.
Group 21A like fenpyroximate: do not rotate the two with each other, and keep it out of ponds.
Group 21A like fenazaquin: do not rotate the two with each other, and keep it out of ponds.
Old broad organophosphate that kills predatory mites. A last resort.

prevent: Plant clean slips and crowns, since the mite rides on planting material. Check their pale bases before planting.
Water in dry months: the mite builds up on drought stressed plants.
Clear old plants and residue before replanting.
Avoid broad insecticides that kill the predatory mites.
bio: Predatory mites and tiny lady beetles feed on the red mite. Spare them.
pests.threshold: In dry months, use a hand lens every two weeks on the pale leaf bases of 5 plants at each of ten spots, and on the crowns of young fruit. Act when live mites and fresh brown patches show on plants in several spots, mostly in the young crop and before flowering.

pests.name: Scale insects of fruit trees
pests.sci: Aspidiotus destructor, Coccus viridis, Lepidosaphes beckii, Chrysomphalus and other scales
pests.hint: Small flat or domed bumps crowd on leaves, twigs and fruits, the plant yellows and weakens, and black sooty mold follows.

sources.label: BPI, Lanzones production guide
ATI 4B, Calamansi production guide
FAO, Avocado production in the Philippines

lanzones: Hits only the moving crawlers. Covered scales survive, and it kills the wasps that keep scales down.
Hits only the moving crawlers. Covered scales survive, and it kills the wasps that keep scales down.
mangosteen: Hits only the moving crawlers. Covered scales survive, and it kills the wasps that keep scales down.
Hits only the moving crawlers. Covered scales survive, and it kills the wasps that keep scales down.
avocado: Hits only the moving crawlers. Covered scales survive, and it kills the wasps that keep scales down.
Hits only the moving crawlers. Covered scales survive, and it kills the wasps that keep scales down.
calamansi: Works on soft scales far better than on hard armored scales. Keep it off flowering trees, it kills bees.
Old, toxic organophosphate. A last resort only, with the full waiting time before harvest.
Hits only the moving crawlers. Covered scales survive, and it kills the wasps that keep scales down.

Old, toxic organophosphate. A last resort only, with the full waiting time before harvest.
Hits only the moving crawlers. Covered scales survive, and it kills the wasps that keep scales down.
Hits only the moving crawlers. Covered scales survive, and it kills the wasps that keep scales down.
guava: Hits only the moving crawlers. Covered scales survive, and it kills the wasps that keep scales down.
