diseases.hint: Thin white pencil lines run along the leaves, the leaves later dry from the tips, and side shoots sprout along the stalk.
diseases.no: Sprays do little once the cane is infected. Plant clean setts of resistant varieties and disinfect cane knives between stools.

sources.label: Recent advances in sugarcane leaf scald disease (PMC)

prevent: Plant resistant varieties, and take setts only from clean nurseries.
Use setts given a long hot water treatment, as for ratoon stunting disease, and planted in a clean nursery.
Disinfect cane knives between stools, with flame, bleach or alcohol, at cutting and at harvest.
Rogue sick stools early, and plow out badly infected ratoons.
Do not move planting material from areas with leaf scald.
diseases.threshold: Inspect seed cane nurseries every month for white pencil lines and leaf tips drying. Any nursery with infected stools should not supply setts. In fields, remove sick stools early and plow out badly hit ratoons.

diseases.name: Heart rot and root rot of pineapple
diseases.hint: The young leaves in the center turn yellow brown, rot at the base and pull out easily with a foul smell.

sources.label: Visayas State University, Major Diseases of Queen Pineapple

pineapple: Dip crowns and slips before planting and spray young plants after long rains. It moves down to the roots.
Dip crowns and slips before planting and spray young plants after long rains. It moves down to the roots.
Group 4 alone breeds resistance fast: use it in a mix or rotate it with a phosphonate.
A weak protectant against this water mold. A late pick.
Labeled for the bacterial heart rot. It only weakly checks Phytophthora.
A weak protectant against this water mold. A late pick.
Copper only weakly checks Phytophthora. The phosphonates do far more.
Labeled for the bacterial heart rot. It only weakly checks Phytophthora.

avoid: Carbendazim
Works on true fungi, not on the water mold behind this heart rot.
Sulfur
A mite and mildew product. It does not stop Phytophthora.
Prochloraz
Works on true fungi, not on the water mold behind this heart rot.
Oxytetracycline
An antibiotic for the bacterial heart rot. It does nothing to Phytophthora.
Plant essential oil
A plant oil blend with no clear proof against Phytophthora.
prevent: Plant on raised beds with good drainage, and keep out of low spots that flood.
Use healthy crowns and slips, cure them in the shade first, and do not bruise them.
Do not plant too deep, and keep rain from splashing soil into the hearts.
Do not lime above the low soil pH pineapple likes. A higher pH favors heart rot.
Pull out and destroy rotted plants, and fix the drainage before replanting the spot.
bio: Trichoderma added to the planting hole or with compost helps hold Phytophthora down.
diseases.threshold: After heavy rains, walk drains and low spots every week and tug the center leaves of any yellowing plant. If they pull out with a foul rot, treat that block. In wet seasons, dip planting material before planting, and protect young plants after long rains where heart rot struck before.
diseases.rotate: Phytophthora quickly resists metalaxyl (group 4) used alone. Alternate it with the phosphonates (fosetyl aluminium, phosphorous acid) or group 40, and prefer the mixes with mancozeb to metalaxyl alone.

diseases.name: Black shank of tobacco
diseases.hint: Plants wilt and stunt, the roots blacken and rot, and the stem turns black from the base, with the dried pith inside often split into discs.

sources.label: AGRIS, Isolation and pathogenicity of Phytophthora from tobacco in Philippine tobacco areas

prevent: Rotate tobacco with corn, rice or other non hosts for three to four years where black shank struck.
Plant resistant varieties where they are sold.
Transplant healthy seedlings from a clean seedbed onto raised, well drained ridges.
Do not move soil or water from sick fields. Clean tools, boots and tractor wheels.
Pull out and burn wilted plants together with their roots.
bio: Trichoderma in the seedbed and the transplant hole helps protect young roots.
diseases.threshold: From transplanting, walk the field every week after rains. In a field with a black shank history, act at the first wilting plants with black stem bases. In clean fields, prevention matters more than any spray.
diseases.rotate: Black shank in tobacco has grown resistant to metalaxyl in fields that used it every year. Pair it with rotation and resistant varieties, and do not use group 4 alone season after season.

diseases.name: Bacterial blight of cotton (angular leaf spot)
diseases.hint: Angular, water soaked spots between the leaf veins turn brown and black, with black streaks along the veins and stems.

sources.label: PhilFIDA, Technoguide on Cotton Pests and their Management

prevent: Plant clean, delinted and treated seed from healthy fields: the bacterium rides on the seed.
Plant resistant varieties where sold.
Plow under crop residue after harvest, and rotate cotton with other crops.
Stay out of the field while the leaves are wet, so you do not spread the bacteria.
Remove volunteer cotton plants between seasons.
diseases.threshold: From the seedling stage to boll set, check the leaves of 20 plants at each of five spots every week, and after every storm. Spray copper early in the attack, when angular spots start to spread in wet, windy weather.

diseases.name: Abaca mosaic
diseases.hint: Light green to yellow streaks and stripes run along the leaf blade, and the plant grows smaller.
diseases.no: No spray cures it. Kill the aphids on the sick mat and on plants within six meters, then remove the whole mat and replant with clean material.

sources.label: DA HVCDP, Giya sa Pagpananum ug Abaca (Technoguide 05, 2019)
JIRCAS, Selected Economically Important Diseases of Some Major Crops in the Philippines

prevent: Plant only virus free corms or tissue culture plantlets from a clean nursery.
Remove sick mats at once: kill the aphids on them first, then kill and dig out the whole mat.
Keep corn, sorghum and grassy weeds such as itch grass away from abaca, since they host the virus and the corn aphid.
Keep a weed free circle around each mat, because weeds harbor the aphids.
Never take suckers from a field that has mosaic.
bio: Lady beetles, hover flies and lacewings eat aphids. They lower the spread but do not stop it.
diseases.threshold: Inspect every mat once a month, and every two weeks in dry, windy months when aphids fly most. Remove each sick mat as soon as the streaks show. For the aphids, act on the colonies on the sick mat and its neighbors before you dig it out.

diseases.name: Abaca bract mosaic
diseases.hint: Leaves curl and roll upward, and the leaf stalks and sheaths show spindle shaped streaks like a cucumber skin.
diseases.no: No spray cures it. Rogue sick plants, keep aphids down and plant only clean, virus free planting material.

sources.label: DA HVCDP, Giya sa Pagpananum ug Abaca (Technoguide 05, 2019)

prevent: Plant only virus free corms or tissue culture plantlets from a clean nursery.
Remove sick plants at once: kill the aphids on them first, then kill and dig out the whole mat.
Remove bananas with bract mosaic near the field, since banana carries the same virus.
Keep the field and a circle around each mat free of weeds that harbor aphids.
Never take suckers from a field that has bract mosaic.
bio: Lady beetles, hover flies and lacewings eat aphids. They lower the spread but do not stop it.
diseases.threshold: Inspect every plant once a month for curled leaves and spindle streaks on the leaf stalks and sheaths. Remove each sick plant at once, after killing the aphids on it and on the plants beside it.

diseases.name: Corynespora leaf fall
diseases.hint: Brown spots with a yellow halo and darkened veins that look like fish bones, and the leaves yellow and fall out of season.

sources.label: DOST PCAARRD, USM study on leaf diseases of rubber in North Cotabato

avoid: Carbendazim
Corynespora resists group 1 fungicides in many crops. Use mancozeb or a group 3 instead.
prevent: Plant clones known to resist Corynespora, and replace or bud over highly susceptible ones.
Feed the trees well after leaf fall, so new leaves come quickly and evenly.
Collect and burn fallen leaves in nurseries and young plantings.
Keep nursery seedlings spaced and their leaves dry, since spores spread in wet weather.
Ease tapping on badly defoliated trees until the canopy recovers.
diseases.threshold: During refoliation after wintering, and all year in nurseries, check the young leaves of 10 trees per hectare every week. Spray the new flush when fishbone spots start to show in wet weather. Old, hardened leaves need no spray.
diseases.rotate: Corynespora cassiicola resists benzimidazoles (group 1) in many crops in Asia. Rely on mancozeb and group 3, and alternate the two.

diseases.name: Bamboo witches broom
diseases.sci: Candidatus Phytoplasma luffae related strain (16SrVIII) in the Philippines, while the fungus Aciculosporium take causes a similar broom elsewhere
diseases.hint: Leaves bunch into rosettes, many thin limbs sprout from one node and the internodes stay short, like a broom.
diseases.no: No spray cures it. Cut and burn the broomed branches and culms, and take planting material only from healthy clumps.

sources.label: Philippine Journal of Science, Distribution of bamboo witches broom disease in the Philippines

prevent: Cut and burn broomed branches and culms as soon as you see them.
Dig out and burn badly broomed clumps whole.
Take culm cuttings, offsets or rhizomes only from healthy clumps.
Clean bolos and saws between clumps with flame, bleach or alcohol.
Do not bring planting material from areas with broom.
diseases.threshold: Check each clump every few months for branches with bunched leaves and many thin twigs from one node. Remove broomed parts the day you find them. A clump that brooms on most culms should go.

diseases.name: Pestalotiopsis leaf fall
diseases.sci: Pestalotiopsis spp. (Pestalotiopsis microspora and other species)
diseases.hint: Round brown spots with a pale yellow ring appear on mature leaves, then the leaves yellow and drop until the canopy is thin and latex output falls.

sources.label: DOST PCAARRD, Addressing the Pestalotiopsis leaf fall disease in rubber trees in Mindanao
Journal News, More funds for treatment of infected rubber plantations in BARMM
Philippine Rubber Research Institute, Pestalotiopsis leaf fall disease in Basilan

rubber: Group 1 carries a high resistance risk: alternate with a protectant or a group 3 product.
The mancozeb part guards against resistance. Spray young trees and nurseries in the wet months.

prevent: Feed the trees well, with enough potassium and magnesium, so they refoliate quickly after leaf fall.
Rest or ease tapping on trees with thin canopies until they recover.
Rake and burn or bury fallen leaves in nurseries and young plantings.
Note which clones hold their leaves in your area, and favor them when you replant.
Keep weeds down and rows open, so the canopy dries after rain.
diseases.threshold: From the start of the wet season, check the canopy of 10 trees per hectare every month for round brown spots with a pale yellow ring and early leaf drop. A spray pays mainly in nurseries and young plantings. In tall trees, feeding and tapping rest come first.

diseases.name: Curvularia leaf spot
diseases.hint: Small yellow spots on young nursery seedlings turn brown with a yellow ring and join into dry patches, and badly hit seedlings stunt or die.
diseases.no: No fungicide for this nursery disease is listed in Philippine guides; space the seedlings, water at the base in the morning, and cut off and burn spotted leaves.

sources.label: Prince of Songkla University, Curvularia leaf spot of oil palm seedlings (2016)

oilpalm: A protectant: spray the healthy seedlings around the spotted ones. It does not heal spots.

prevent: Space the polybags so the leaves do not touch and air moves between them.
Water at the base in the morning, not on the leaves late in the day.
Cut off and burn spotted leaves, and remove badly hit seedlings.
Feed the seedlings in balance. Starved or overfed seedlings spot more.
Use clean, well drained potting soil, and keep grass weeds out of the nursery.
diseases.threshold: Check nursery seedlings every week, above all in the first months. Act when spots show on more than a few seedlings in a bed: cut off the spotted leaves and protect the rest.

diseases.name: Sooty mold
diseases.sci: Capnodium mangiferae, Capnodium ramosum and other sooty mold fungi
diseases.hint: A black velvety coat like soot covers leaves, flowers and fruit wherever leafhoppers, scales or mealybugs drip sticky honeydew.
diseases.no: A fungicide on the black coat does little. Control the honeydew insects, keep ants off the trees and prune for light and air. The mold then fades.

sources.label: DA Caraga HVCDP, Giya sa pagpananum ug manga
BPI, Mangosteen production guide

prevent: Find and control the insect that drips the honeydew (leafhoppers, scales, mealybugs, aphids or whiteflies). The mold fades once the honeydew stops.
Keep ants off the trees with sticky bands on the trunk and by cutting branches that touch the ground. Ants guard the honeydew insects.
Prune for light and air so the canopy dries fast and natural enemies reach the insects.
A spray of mild soap in water or a horticultural oil loosens the black coat so rain washes it off.
Wash or wipe sooty fruit after harvest. The coat sits only on the skin.
bio: Ladybird beetles, lacewings and tiny wasps clean up scales, mealybugs and aphids once the ants are kept away.
diseases.threshold: Look at leaves and fruit for the black coat and, under it, for the insects that feed it: leafhoppers in mango flowers, scales and mealybugs on twigs, and ants running up the trunk. Act on the insects once the coat spreads over many leaves or onto the fruit.

diseases.name: Pink disease
diseases.hint: White cobweb threads, then a pink crust, cover the branches near the forks, and the leaves above die but stay hanging.

sources.label: Pacific Pests and Pathogens, Pink disease of cocoa
DA HVCDP and BPI DNCRDC, Durian production guide

prevent: Check branch forks often in the rains. The white cobweb stage is the time to act, before the pink crust forms.
Cut sick branches at least 30 cm below the last sign of the fungus, in dry weather, and take them out of the farm.
Brush copper paste on the cut ends and on early patches on the trunk or the main fork.
Thin heavy shade and space trees well, at least 3 meters for cacao, so the canopy dries after rain.
Keep trees well fed. Stressed, crowded trees catch pink disease more easily.
diseases.threshold: In the rainy months, check the branch forks every two weeks for white cobweb threads and pink crust. Act at the cobweb stage, before the bark cracks. A branch with dead leaves hanging on it must be cut.

diseases.name: Phytophthora patch canker, foot rot and fruit rot
diseases.hint: Wet dark patches on the trunk bark ooze reddish brown gum, seedlings die back, and fruits get water soaked spots that turn brown, crack and rot.

sources.label: BPI, Durian production guide
DA HVCDP and BPI DNCRDC, Durian production guide
DOST PCAARRD, ACIAR jackfruit project on Phytophthora

durian: Groups 43 and P07: use it as the label says and rotate with copper. It protects, it does not rebuild rotten bark.
papaya: Group 40: rotate with a phosphonate or copper. Do not lean on it season after season.
Group 4: water molds learn to resist it fast. Never use it alone, rotate with copper or a phosphonate.
A plant oil product: weak against water molds. Keep it as a minor partner.

prevent: Plant on well drained ground or on mounds, and dig drains so water never stands around the trunk.
Keep mulch, weeds and soil a hand away from the trunk base, and avoid wounding the trunk with tools.
Scrape bark patches to clean wood in dry weather and paint the wound with copper paste. Burn the scrapings.
Prune low branches and remove fruit near the ground. Rain splash from the soil carries the water mold up.
Pick and bury rotting and fallen fruit, and do not plant papaya next to cacao or durian blocks that have the disease.
Plant seedlings grafted high on tolerant rootstocks and raised in clean, well drained nursery soil.
bio: Trichoderma mixed into compost around the root zone can hold soil water molds down. It helps, but it does not cure trunk cankers.
diseases.threshold: After heavy rain, check trunks near the ground and the branch forks for wet dark patches that ooze reddish gum, and young fruit for water soaked spots. Act on the first patch: scrape it to clean wood and treat it, and pick rotting fruit at once.
diseases.rotate: Water molds learn to resist metalaxyl (group 4) quickly when it is used alone. Mix or rotate it with copper, fosetyl (P07), dimethomorph (40) or fluopicolide (43).

diseases.name: Algal leaf spot
diseases.hint: Fuzzy round green to orange spots on the upper side of the leaves, and black rough spots on guava fruit.
diseases.no: Spraying is seldom worth it. Prune low branches, open the canopy to light and air, drain wet ground and feed the trees well.

sources.label: Pacific Pests and Pathogens, Algal leaf spot

mango: Copper clears the alga on hard hit trees, but pruning, light and feeding do more. Spray only when the spots keep spreading.

prevent: Prune low hanging branches and thin the canopy so light and air reach the inner leaves.
Drain waterlogged ground and keep weeds down around the trees to lower the damp.
Feed weak trees. The alga hits poorly growing trees hardest.
Thin shade trees that keep cacao and coffee too dark and wet.
In wet areas, space guava trees wide, with rows that let the wind pass.
diseases.threshold: In the wet season, check low and shaded branches. Act when the fuzzy orange spots spread over many leaves or show on guava fruit. A few spots on old leaves need no action.

diseases.name: White root rot
diseases.hint: Leaves lose their gloss, turn yellow, curl down and fall, and thick white threads cover the roots and the collar, with orange brackets at the base later.

sources.label: Rubber Research Institute of Sri Lanka, Management of White Root Disease

prevent: When clearing land, dig out and burn old stumps and roots of forest trees and old rubber. They carry the fungus into the new planting.
Sow legume cover crops between the rows. They speed the rotting of buried roots and starve the fungus.
In the first years, open the soil at the collar of trees near a sick one every few months and remove white threads early.
Dig a trench around a group of sick trees to cut root contact with healthy ones.
Remove dead trees with their roots and burn them. Leave the hole open to dry before you replant.
bio: Trichoderma mixed with compost in the planting hole and around the collar helps keep the fungus off new roots.
diseases.threshold: Around any yellowing or dead tree, scrape the soil from the collar and the main roots of its neighbors and look for white threads stuck to the bark. Treat every tree whose collar shows threads, and check again every few months.

diseases.name: Citrus tristeza
diseases.hint: Trees slowly decline with small yellowing leaves, twig dieback and pits in the wood under the bark, often together with greening.
diseases.no: No spray cures it. Plant certified virus free seedlings on tolerant rootstock, remove declining trees and keep aphids off nurseries and budwood trees.

sources.label: Philippine Agricultural Scientist, HLB and tristeza in Oriental Mindoro calamansi

prevent: Plant certified virus free seedlings grafted on tristeza tolerant rootstock. Never graft budwood from an untested tree.
Keep budwood mother trees and nurseries in insect proof screen houses and keep aphids off them.
Replace declining trees, or a whole block once it no longer pays, with clean trees on tolerant rootstock.
Never move citrus plants or budwood from declining orchards into clean areas.
bio: Ladybird beetles, lacewings, hoverflies and small wasps keep citrus aphids down. They slow the spread but cannot stop the virus.
diseases.threshold: In nurseries and on budwood mother trees, check new flushes every week for aphid colonies and keep them clean. In the orchard, watch for trees that slowly decline with small yellow leaves and pits in the wood under the bark.

diseases.name: Citrus foot rot and gummosis
diseases.sci: Phytophthora spp. (Phytophthora citrophthora, Phytophthora nicotianae, Phytophthora palmivora)
diseases.hint: Dark sticky gum oozes from cracked bark near the base of the trunk, the bark underneath turns brown and rots, and the canopy yellows and thins.

sources.label: ATI 4B, Calamansi production guide

pomelo: Groups 43 and P07: use it as the label says and rotate with copper on the trunk. It does not heal dead bark.

prevent: Plant on well drained ground or on mounds and dig drains. Citrus collars rot in standing water.
Use seedlings budded high on a tolerant rootstock, so rain splash from the soil does not reach the scion bark.
Keep grass, mulch and soil off the trunk base, and avoid hoe and brush cutter wounds there.
Prune low branches to about 1 meter above the soil, so splash and damp stay off the leaves and fruit.
Scrape a gumming patch to clean wood in dry weather and paint it with copper paste. Burn the scrapings.
Water at the base without wetting the trunk, and never let water pool around it.
bio: Trichoderma in compost around the root zone helps hold soil water molds down. It does not cure trunk cankers.
diseases.threshold: Each month in the rains and after every flood, look at the trunk base of each tree, above all in the first 2 years. Act on the first patch of gum or dark wet bark.
diseases.rotate: Water molds learn to resist metalaxyl (group 4) quickly when it is used alone. Rotate it with fosetyl (P07), copper or fluopicolide (43).

diseases.name: Citrus scab
diseases.hint: Raised corky pale orange to brown warts form on young leaves, twigs and fruits, and badly hit leaves crinkle and twist.

sources.label: ATI 4B, Calamansi production guide

calamansi: Spray as new flushes push and again as petals fall. Scab only enters young leaves and fruit.
Spray as new flushes push and again as petals fall. Scab only enters young leaves and fruit.
Group 1: scab fungi have resisted it where it was overused. Limit it to 2 sprays a season and rotate with copper.
Group 1: scab fungi have resisted it where it was overused. Limit it to 2 sprays a season and rotate with copper.
Toxic to fish: keep it out of streams and ponds.
A home made copper that must be mixed fresh and right, or it scorches young leaves. Ready copper products are easier.
citrus: Spray as new flushes push and again as petals fall. Scab only enters young leaves and fruit.
Spray as new flushes push and again as petals fall. Scab only enters young leaves and fruit.
Group 1: scab fungi have resisted it where it was overused. Limit it to 2 sprays a season and rotate with copper.
Group 1: scab fungi have resisted it where it was overused. Limit it to 2 sprays a season and rotate with copper.
Toxic to fish: keep it out of streams and ponds.
A home made copper that must be mixed fresh and right, or it scorches young leaves. Ready copper products are easier.
pomelo: Spray as new flushes push and again as petals fall. Scab only enters young leaves and fruit.
Spray as new flushes push and again as petals fall. Scab only enters young leaves and fruit.
Group 1: scab fungi have resisted it where it was overused. Limit it to 2 sprays a season and rotate with copper.
Group 1: scab fungi have resisted it where it was overused. Limit it to 2 sprays a season and rotate with copper.
Toxic to fish: keep it out of streams and ponds.
A home made copper that must be mixed fresh and right, or it scorches young leaves. Ready copper products are easier.
Groups 7 and 11: no two sprays in a row. Rotate with copper.
A biological: weak alone in the rains. Use it beside copper and pruning.

prevent: Raise rootstocks and budwood away from scabby orchards, and protect nursery flushes. Scabby seedlings grow stunted and hard to bud.
Prune each year for an open canopy, cut out dead wood and remove scabby twigs.
Water at the base, not over the canopy, and avoid crowding trees.
Time fertilizer so flushes come in drier weeks where you can. Young flush in the rain is what scab needs.
diseases.threshold: Watch each new flush and the fruit set: scab only infects young tissue in wet weather. Protect when a flush pushes or petals fall during rainy weeks, above all in nurseries and on calamansi and pomelo with scab last season.
diseases.rotate: Scab fungi in heavily sprayed citrus groves abroad became resistant to group 1 (benomyl, thiophanate methyl). Use group 1 at most twice a season and rotate it with copper.

diseases.name: Citrus canker
diseases.hint: Raised corky brown spots with a yellow ring and an oily, glazed edge appear on leaves, twigs and fruits.

sources.label: ATI 4B, Calamansi production guide

calamansi: Best on young fruit and new flushes before rain. It protects, it does not heal spots already there.
Best on young fruit and new flushes before rain. It protects, it does not heal spots already there.
A home made copper that must be mixed fresh and right, or it scorches young leaves. Ready copper products are easier.
citrus: Best on young fruit and new flushes before rain. It protects, it does not heal spots already there.
Best on young fruit and new flushes before rain. It protects, it does not heal spots already there.
A home made copper that must be mixed fresh and right, or it scorches young leaves. Ready copper products are easier.
pomelo: Best on young fruit and new flushes before rain. It protects, it does not heal spots already there.
Best on young fruit and new flushes before rain. It protects, it does not heal spots already there.
A home made copper that must be mixed fresh and right, or it scorches young leaves. Ready copper products are easier.
A biological: weak alone against canker in windy, rainy weather. Use it beside copper and pruning.

prevent: Plant canker free seedlings from a clean nursery, and do not bring in budwood or seedlings from sick orchards.
Plant windbreaks around and across the orchard. Wind driven rain spreads canker and makes the wounds it enters.
Prune and burn twigs with canker in dry weather, and clean the shears between trees.
Keep citrus leafminer down on new flushes. Its tunnels let canker in.
Stay out of the orchard while the trees are wet, and water at the base instead of over the leaves.
diseases.threshold: Check new flushes and young fruit every week or two in the rains, more after storms. Act when the first raised corky spots with a yellow ring show on young leaves or fruit: prune them out in dry weather and protect the next flush and the young fruit.

diseases.name: Diplodia fruit rot
diseases.hint: Fruits darken to brown and black from the stem end or a wound, the flesh turns dry and corky, and black sooty spores cover the skin.

sources.label: PROSEA via Growables, Star apple diseases and pests
Horticulturae (MDPI), Lasiodiplodia and other fungi on soursop fruit

prevent: Bag young fruit early with paper or net bags. Bags keep spores off and stop the insect wounds where the rot starts.
Prune dead twigs and branches, which carry the fungus, and burn them with any mummified fruit left on the tree.
Pick up fallen and rotting fruit every few days and bury it away from the trees.
Harvest with a short stalk, handle gently and keep the fruit cool and dry. The rot starts at the stem end and at bruises.
Keep trees watered in long dry spells and well fed. Stressed trees die back and feed the fungus.
diseases.threshold: Check the fruit every week from fruit set. Remove any fruit that darkens from the stem end or around a wound, and look for black dieback on the twigs that feed the rot.

diseases.name: Burrowing nematode and root lesion nematodes of banana
diseases.sci: Radopholus similis, Pratylenchus coffeae, Pratylenchus goodeyi
diseases.hint: Roots show dark red to black lesions and snap easily, plants stay small with light bunches, and heavy plants topple over in wind or rain.

sources.label: BPI, Banana production guide
DA HVCDP, Banana production manual

banana: Counts as one of the year's group 7 sprays in the black sigatoka program. Do not add more group 7 leaf sprays that year.
An organophosphate: wear gloves and boots, keep it out of water, and treat only mats in fields where nematodes cut yield.
Extremely toxic to people, birds and fish: full protective wear, never near water or where animals graze. A last resort.
A biological: works best with compost and clean plantlets. Alone it only slows the nematodes.
Highly toxic to people and to fish: full protective wear, never near water. A last resort.
Highly toxic to people: full protective wear. A last resort.

prevent: Plant tissue culture plantlets, or pare suckers to clean white tissue and dip them 20 to 30 seconds in boiling water before planting.
On worn out ground, rest the field 10 to 12 months with no banana or weeds, or rotate with pineapple, then replant clean plantlets.
Grow sunn hemp (Crotalaria) or marigold as a cover crop before banana. They hold nematode numbers down.
Work compost or manure into the soil and mulch the mats. More roots grow and soil life eats the nematodes.
Prop heavy bearing plants with bamboo poles in nematode ground so they do not topple before harvest.
Open drains in wet ground. Waterlogged roots rot faster where nematodes feed.
bio: Soil fungi and bacteria that attack nematodes (Purpureocillium, Trichoderma, Bacillus) do best in compost rich soil. They slow the nematodes but do not clear them.
diseases.threshold: Before replanting and every few months, dig beside a few plants and split some roots lengthwise: red brown to black streaks in the outer root, many dead roots, small bunches or plants that topple mean the nematodes are costing yield. Treat or rest the field when many plants show this.
diseases.rotate: Soils treated again and again with the same organophosphate or carbamate nematicide learn to break it down fast, so it stops working. Rotate between fluopyram and an organophosphate, and lean on clean plantlets and fallow.

diseases.name: Banana bract mosaic
diseases.hint: Spindle shaped streaks run along the leaves and leaf stalks, and the heart bracts and inner leaf sheaths show a dark reddish brown mosaic, mostly on saba and latundan.
diseases.no: No spray cures it. Kill the aphids on a sick mat, destroy the whole mat, keep corn and weeds away and replant clean tissue culture plantlets.

sources.label: BPI, Banana production guide
DA HVCDP, Banana production manual

prevent: Plant only virus tested tissue culture plantlets. Never take suckers from a mat with streaked leaf stalks or mottled bracts.
Kill aphids on a sick mat first, then destroy the whole mat and its suckers with herbicide or by digging it out and chopping it.
Do not grow corn next to banana. Aphids from the corn carry the virus to the mats.
Keep weeds down around the mats and prune extra suckers, where aphids gather.
Remove sick mats early and check the neighbors every two weeks for the next months.
bio: Ladybird beetles, hoverfly larvae and small wasps eat aphids, but they never stop the virus. Spray only the sick mat to spare them.
diseases.threshold: Check each mat every two weeks, mostly saba and latundan: peel back an old leaf sheath and look for spindle streaks on the leaf stalks and a reddish brown mosaic on the inner sheaths and heart bracts. One sick mat means act that day.

diseases.name: Banana freckle
diseases.hint: Older leaves and the fruit peel get many tiny raised black dots that feel rough like sandpaper, and the blemished fruit sells poorly.

sources.label: BPI, Banana production guide
DA HVCDP, Banana production manual

banana: A strong protectant for leaves and fruit. Keep it out of streams because it is toxic to fish.
Group 11: at most 3 sprays a year with your sigatoka sprays, always mixed, never two in a row.
Group 7: at most 3 sprays a year with your sigatoka sprays, always mixed, never two in a row.
Group 11: at most 3 sprays a year with your sigatoka sprays, always mixed, never two in a row.
Group 10: always mixed with a protectant, at most 3 sprays a year.
Group 1: the fungus learns fast. At most 3 sprays a year, mixed, never two in a row.
An old protectant that is harsh on skin and eyes. Other protectants do the job better.
An older group 3 fungicide. Newer ones in the same group work better.
Weak on freckle. At most a minor partner.

avoid: Potassium silicate
A plant tonic, not a fungicide: it does not stop the freckle fungus.
prevent: Bag each bunch soon after the male bud is removed. The bag keeps spores off the peel.
Cut off old leaves with freckle dots, above all those hanging over the bunch, and take them out of the field.
Keep the black sigatoka program going. The same protectant sprays hold freckle too.
Plant clean tissue culture plantlets and never move leaves or suckers from farms with freckle.
Desucker and keep wide spacing so air moves and the leaves dry fast.
diseases.threshold: In the wet months, check the leaves hanging over each bunch and the young fruit every week. Act when tiny black sandpaper dots show on those leaves or on the peel: cut the spotted leaves and bag the bunch.
diseases.rotate: Count every freckle spray in the same yearly limits as black sigatoka: mix each systemic with a protectant, never one group twice in a row, and about 3 sprays a year for groups 1, 7 and 11.

diseases.name: Papaya bacterial crown rot
diseases.hint: Angular water soaked spots on leaves and leaf stalks spread into a soft rot of the crown, the top of the plant collapses, and fruits get firm sunken spots.
diseases.no: No spray reliably cures it. Cut out and bury sick plants at once, avoid wounding plants, clean your tools and plant tolerant lines.

sources.label: UPLB, Erwinia mallotivora and papaya bacterial crown rot
ACIAR, Papaya and fruit disease final report HORT 2012 113

papaya: May slow the spread to nearby plants after you cut out the sick ones. It cannot save a crown that is already rotting.

prevent: Cut out sick plants the same day, bury them deep or carry them off, and only then think of spraying the rest.
Avoid wounding leaves and stems. Remove old leaves with a clean cut in dry weather.
Dip knives in household bleach mixed with water between plants.
Plant tolerant varieties where the disease is common, and buy seedlings from clean nurseries.
Do not plant new papaya next to sick blocks, and plant in drier months when you can. The bacterium spreads in wind and rain.
diseases.threshold: In wet, windy weather, walk the field twice a week and look for water soaked angular spots on leaves and leaf stalks near the crown. Remove a plant at the first soft rot at the top. Do not wait for a second one.

diseases.name: Mango scab
diseases.hint: Young fruits get grey brown corky spots that roughen and twist the skin, and leaves show brown rough spots on the underside.

sources.label: DA Caraga HVCDP, Giya sa pagpananum ug manga

mango: The anthracnose protectant program covers scab too. Keep young leaves and fruit covered in rainy weeks.
Groups 11 and 3 together: switch to a protectant or another group between sprays.
Group 11 alone invites resistance: never two in a row, best mixed or rotated with mancozeb.
The mancozeb part carries it where the fungus resists group 1. Still rotate.
An old protectant that is harsh on skin and eyes. Mancozeb does the same job.

prevent: Prune after harvest to open the canopy, and cut out scabby twigs and leaves that carry the fungus to the next flush.
Protect nursery seedlings and grafts. Scab stunts young plants and travels on them to new orchards.
Induce flowering for a dry stretch where you can. Fruit set in rain catches scab and anthracnose together.
Rake and burn fallen scabby leaves and fruit.
Bag the fruit on time. The bag keeps late infections and fruit flies off.
diseases.threshold: Scab only infects young leaves, flowers and young fruit in wet weather. Protect each new flush and the fruit set during rainy weeks, above all in nurseries and on trees that had scab last season.

diseases.name: Rhizopus fruit rot of jackfruit
diseases.hint: Male flowers and young fruits turn soft and brown, get covered with grey black fuzzy mold, and then drop.
diseases.no: Sprays are seldom needed. Pick off sick flowers and fruit, prune for air, and handle the fruit gently.

sources.label: Vikaspedia, IPM for jackfruit pests

prevent: Prune the trees open so wind dries the young fruit quickly after rain.
Remove rotting male spikes and young fruit from the tree and the ground, and bury them away from the trees.
Harvest and carry fruit with care. Bruises and cuts let the mold in.
Store fruit in a cool, airy place, and pull out a rotting fruit at once before it spreads to the rest.
Keep packing sheds, crates and bins clean of old fruit and plant trash.
diseases.threshold: In the rains, check the male flower spikes and young fruit every week. Pick off any that turn soft and brown or carry grey black fuzz, and gather the ones on the ground.

diseases.name: Avocado root rot
diseases.hint: Leaves turn pale, small and wilted, branches die back from the top and feeder roots are black and rotten, worst on wet poorly drained soil.

sources.label: FAO, Avocado production in the Philippines

prevent: Plant only on deep, well drained soil, and on mounds or ridges where water may stand after rain.
Buy seedlings from a clean nursery with healthy white roots, grafted on a tolerant rootstock where you can get one.
Keep a thick, coarse mulch of wood chips or dry leaves under the canopy, away from the trunk. It feeds soil life that holds the water mold down.
Water with care: never keep the soil soggy, and fix leaks and blocked drains.
Do not bring mud from sick orchards on boots, tools or seedling bags.
bio: Coarse organic mulch and compost raise the soil life that competes with the water mold. Trichoderma products can be added at planting.
diseases.threshold: After long rains, check trees for thin pale canopies, small wilted leaves and dieback from the top. Dig gently under the drip line: black, brittle feeder roots mean act at once on drainage and treatment.
diseases.rotate: Water molds learn to resist metalaxyl (group 4) with repeated use. Rely on phosphonate for older trees and keep metalaxyl for nurseries and young plantings.

diseases.name: Avocado scab
diseases.hint: Raised brown corky scabs form on young fruits and leaves and later merge into rough patches on the skin.

sources.label: FAO, Avocado production in the Philippines

prevent: Prune to open the canopy so leaves and fruit dry quickly after rain.
Pick off and burn scabby fruit and leaves, and rake up the fallen ones.
Water at the base, not over the canopy.
Plant less susceptible varieties where scab is common.
diseases.threshold: In wet weather, check new leaves and young fruit every week from fruit set. Act when the first raised corky spots appear on young fruit. Older fruit no longer catch scab.

diseases.name: Rambutan powdery mildew
diseases.hint: White powdery growth covers young flushes, flowers and young fruits, which turn brown, grow short spines, stay small and drop.

sources.label: BPI Davao, Powdery mildew of rambutan (FAO AGRIS)

prevent: Prune after harvest so light and air reach the inner canopy.
Cut out and burn badly hit flower clusters and young shoots.
Feed balanced fertilizer. Too much nitrogen gives soft, lush flushes that mildew loves.
Keep trees watered in dry spells, so flowering stays even and short.
diseases.threshold: From bud break, check new flushes and flower clusters twice a week, mostly in dry months with cool, dewy nights. Act at the first white powder on flowers or young fruit. Once young fruit turn brown and drop, the loss is done.

diseases.name: Vascular streak dieback of cacao
diseases.hint: Leaves two or three behind the shoot tip turn yellow with small green spots and fall within days, and the branch dies back with brown streaks in the wood.
diseases.no: No spray controls it well. Cut infected branches 30 cm below the streaks and burn them, thin the shade and plant tolerant clones.

sources.label: BPI, Cacao production guide
Pacific Pests and Pathogens, Cocoa vascular streak dieback

prevent: Plant tolerant clones. On susceptible trees pruning alone rarely keeps up.
Cut infected branches about 30 cm below the last brown streak in the wood, in dry weather, and burn them.
Raise nurseries far from older cacao or under cover. Spores from sick trees land on young seedling flushes.
Thin heavy shade and prune regularly so the canopy dries after rain.
Do not move budwood or seedlings from areas with the disease to clean ones.
diseases.threshold: Every two weeks in the rains, look at the second and third leaves behind each shoot tip: yellow leaves with small green spots that drop within days mean that branch is infected. Split the twig: brown streaks in the wood confirm it.

diseases.name: Dragon fruit stem canker
diseases.hint: Small sunken white or orange spots on the stems become rusty brown corky cankers that crack and leave holes, and fruits get spots too.

sources.label: UPLB, Dragon fruit stem canker and its control

prevent: Cut out and burn sick stem pieces, cutting into healthy tissue, and dip the knife in bleach water between cuts.
Plant cuttings from canker free plants, and let the cut ends dry a week before planting.
Do not water over the plants. Water at the base in the morning and keep the beds well drained.
Go easy on nitrogen. Soft, lush stems catch canker most.
Clear fallen stems and fruit from under the posts, and thin crowded stems so air moves.
bio: Bacillus based biologicals sprayed on new growth can slow the canker in drier weeks. They do not cure cankers.
diseases.threshold: In the rains, check the young stems every week for small sunken white or orange spots. Cut those segments out at once and protect the new growth before the next rain.

diseases.name: Chico leaf spot
diseases.hint: The leaves fill with tiny spots, pinkish to reddish brown, each with a pale whitish middle.

sources.label: National Horticulture Board India, Sapota diseases

prevent: Rake up and burn fallen spotted leaves.
Prune for light and air so the leaves dry fast after rain.
Feed trees well. Weak trees lose more leaves to spots.
In nurseries, space seedlings and water at the base instead of over the leaves.
diseases.threshold: Act only when spots cover many leaves and trees drop leaves early, mostly in nurseries and young trees. A few spots on old leaves need nothing.
